issues.legal_issue: The authority to determine whether land claimed by a jagirdar is khudkasht lies exclusively with the authority assigned to decide the character of property in the jagir-resumption scheme, rather than with revenue authorities deciding record-entry disputes.
material_facts: After resumption of the jagir, the jagirdar claimed agricultural land as khudkasht and sought correction of revenue-record entries.
The requested correction depended on deciding whether the land was khudkasht.
The revenue authorities directed changes to the entries without first obtaining a decision on the land’s character from the designated jagir authority.
issues.conclusion: The jagir authority had exclusive jurisdiction to determine whether the land was khudkasht. The revenue-record entries could be considered for correction only after that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 23(1) and 23(2) of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952, a question about whether property has the specified character must be referred to the Jagir Commissioner for the prescribed inquiry. Sections 46 and 47 bar other courts and authorities from deciding matters assigned under the Act and give the Act and its rules precedence over inconsistent laws. Sections 125 and 136 of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 empower revenue authorities to decide disputes about entries, but not to determine whether a jagirdar’s claimed land is khudkasht. Section 23 is independent of section 37, which addresses different questions of title and related matters. The Court applied the principle in Barker v. Edger, [1898] A.C. 748, that a later general enactment does not impliedly displace an earlier special enactment.

predicates.khudkasht_claim_in_jagir_resumption_proc: A jagirdar claims land as khudkasht in a proceeding arising from resumption of a jagir.
predicates.property_character_is_disputed: The parties dispute whether the claimed land has the character of khudkasht property.
predicates.entry_correction_depends_on_property_cha: A requested change to revenue-record entries depends on deciding whether the land is khudkasht.

issues.definition: When a khudkasht claim in a jagir-resumption proceeding presents a disputed property-character issue on which an entry correction depends, the designated jagir authority has exclusive power to decide that issue.

issues.legal_issue: An inquiry into a jagirdar’s claim that property is personal property must follow the statutory notice, hearing, and inquiry procedure, and failure to do so supports remand for a compliant inquiry.
material_facts: The jagir authority delegated the inquiry into the claimed property to a subordinate officer.

The subordinate officer fixed the hearing less than two months after receiving the matter, did not give the prescribed notices, and submitted a report without conducting the inquiry in the prescribed manner.
The Board of Revenue set aside the resulting decision and remanded the matter for a proper inquiry under the statutory rules.
issues.conclusion: The Board of Revenue was right to require compliance with the statutory rules and to remand the matter for a fresh inquiry; the High Court erred in quashing that remand.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(2) of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952 requires the prescribed inquiry into whether property is of the nature specified in section 23(1). Rules 23 and 24 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagir Rules, 1954 prescribe the hearing date and notice requirements, while rule 28 requires a reasonable opportunity to prove or disprove the parties’ contentions and an inquiry in the manner provided for the trial of a suit by a Revenue Court. The Jagir Commissioner may entrust the inquiry to a qualified subordinate officer, but that officer must follow the prescribed procedure.

predicates.jagir_personal_property_inquiry: An authority is inquiring into a jagirdar’s claim that property is personal property in a jagir-resumption matter.
predicates.hearing_set_less_than_two_months_after_o: The authority sets the inquiry hearing for a date less than two months after its order fixing the hearing.
predicates.prescribed_notices_not_given: The authority fails to give the notices required for the inquiry to the affected participants or officials.
predicates.prescribed_inquiry_procedure_not_followe: The officer conducting the inquiry fails to follow the required procedure, including giving a reasonable opportunity to contest the claim and conducting the inquiry in the prescribed manner.

issues.definition: If a jagir personal-property inquiry is conducted with an impermissibly early hearing, missing required notices, or a failure to follow the required inquiry procedure, remand for a procedurally compliant inquiry is proper.
